summary.text: A phase transition is a change of a substance from one state to another, most often among solid, liquid and gas.
It happens when conditions such as temperature or pressure change, and some properties can jump abruptly, like the volume when a liquid turns to gas.
At the exact transition point the two phases are equally likely to exist, and on either side one of them is the more stable.

facts.label: What triggers it
facts.value: A change in temperature or pressure

facts.label: Boiling jump
facts.value: Liquid turning to gas changes volume abruptly

facts.label: Phase diagram
facts.value: Shows the most stable phase at each temperature and pressure

facts.label: Solid to solid
facts.value: A crystal can change structure without changing chemistry

facts.label: Magnetic example
facts.value: Ferromagnet to paramagnet at the Curie point

items.prompt: A pot of water sits at the exact temperature where steam and water are equally ready to exist. What is true of the two forms there?

options.label: They have identical free energies, so neither is favored
The water is more stable until the pot empties
The steam is always the more stable of the two
Only one can exist until the heat is turned up

items.explain: At the transition point the two phases have identical free energies, so they are equally likely to exist.

items.prompt: A pot of water is held just under its boiling point. Which form of the water is the more stable one?

options.label: The vapor, because it holds more energy
Neither, since both are equally stable there
The liquid, because the temperature is below boiling
The vapor, because pressure favors it

items.explain: Below the boiling point the liquid is the more stable state; above it the gas is.

items.prompt: Very clean water is chilled a few degrees past its freezing point and stays unfrozen. How is this state best described?

options.label: Unstable, so it must freeze immediately
Metastable: less stable than ice, yet not unstable
Fully stable, the same as ice at that point
A plasma, because it passed the transition

items.explain: Supercooling carries a system past a transition point without the transition; the result is metastable.

items.prompt: Carbon, a pure element, rearranges from one crystal structure to another with no change in chemistry. What is this kind of change called?

options.label: Polymorphism
Supersaturation
A eutectic transformation
Allotropy

items.explain: In elements a change of crystal structure is allotropy; in compounds it is polymorphism.

items.prompt: A magnetic material switches from ferromagnetic to paramagnetic. What is the temperature of this change called?

options.label: The Curie point
The boiling point
The spinodal point
The eutectoid point

items.explain: The ferromagnetic to paramagnetic transition occurs at the Curie point.

items.prompt: A lab heats a pure compound and watches it melt. What is typical of a chemically pure compound?

options.label: It melts across a span where solid and liquid coexist
It has separate liquidus and solidus temperatures
It melts at a single temperature
It melts only when pressure is also changed

items.explain: Pure compounds show one melting temperature, while mixtures may have a span between solidus and liquidus.
